key_insight: UniAIR is a unified multimodal AI framework that predicts the effects of mutations across antibody, antigen and T-cell receptor recognition by learning shared representations that generalize across adaptive-immune tasks.
problem_solved: Bridges fragmented, task-specific mutation-effect models by enabling a single model to generalize mutation-impact predictions across diverse immune receptors and antigens, addressing limited transferability and sparse labeled data across modalities.
method: Unified multimodal encoder that integrates diverse inputs (e.g., protein sequence and structural/contextual features) into a shared representation space.
Cross-task training and shared latent embeddings to transfer knowledge across antibody, antigen and TCR prediction tasks, improving generalization to unseen mutations and targets.
Task-specific decoders or heads for mutation-effect scoring while leveraging joint supervision to align functional signals across immune recognition modalities.
impact: Provides a reusable blueprint for building generalizable, multimodal bioinformatics models that transfer across related biological tasks—useful for practitioners working on protein design, vaccine development, and cross-domain representation learning.
visual_elements: Schematic of the UniAIR architecture showing a shared encoder with separate task heads for antibody, antigen, and TCR outputs.
Diagram illustrating multimodal inputs (sequence, structure, context) merging into a common embedding space.
Bar/line chart comparing mutation-effect prediction performance of UniAIR vs baseline task-specific models.
Embedding visualization (e.g., UMAP) showing clustering/alignment of immune receptor and antigen representations before and after joint training.
paper_title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework
paper_authors: Rong Han, Yumeng Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Lei Fu, Tong Pan
